> A 3-part 3D-printed chassis for the Buddy robot, designed in Onshape and exported as STEP/STL. Part 1 — Base tub: houses the ESP32 on standoffs, motor mounts for the drive motors, and a power-bank bay for battery power. Part 2 — Face frame: fits the display with a display window cutout plus a slot for the RGB LED strip. Part 3 — Top shell: button holes for user input and a speaker grille. All parts designed with 3D-printing tolerances in mind so they fit together and mount the Week 1 electronics.

## Design

### 2026-10-12 – # Week 2 CAD: Buddy chassis modeled, exported, and imported to Onshape

**6h**

# Week 2 CAD: Buddy chassis modeled, exported, and imported to Onshape

Designed the 3-part 3D-printed chassis for the Buddy robot as a fully parametric CadQuery model (buddy_chassis.py: change a dimension, re-run, get new files).

Part 1: Base tub (160x120x40mm): 4x M3 ESP32 standoffs, 2x TT motor plinths with shaft holes through the side walls, USB power-bank bay, rocker-switch slot and USB-C opening in the rear wall, wire channels, 4x full-height M3 corner pillars for the lid screws.

Part 2: Face frame: display window cutout for the 1.47" ST7789, RGB light-pipe slot, 4x display mount posts, 2x M3 mounting holes to the base front wall.

Part 3: Top shell: 3x tact-button holes, speaker grille (2.5mm hole array) over a 40mm speaker pocket with air cavity, MAX98357A mount posts, INMP441 mic pinhole + posts, 4x corner screw holes, alignment lip.

### 2026-10-15 – # Week 2 continued: repo finished

**4h**

# Week 2 continued: repo finished

Put 4 hours into finishing the Week 2 repo after the CAD work.

First rewrote the README from scratch with image guides and descriptions for every CAD view. No code in the repo, images and descriptions only.

Then wrote up the docs: the BOM draft with the Tier 1 math, the journal draft, and the final design notes.

The long part was publishing everything. All 23 files went up as 30 separate commits, one file at a time, each verified after pushing: 6 Onshape screenshots, 5 geometry previews, 5 Blender renders, 3 STEP exports, 3 STL exports, 2 reels.

Also finished the BOM.
